doc_friction.issue: redteam.py targets did not list shift-roster-builder/import-shifts.mjs (or calc.mjs) though their suite is the venture glob; with --target the campaign ran the whole 449-test venture suite (~160 s per mutant, ~22 min for 8, and rerun ~16 min). A per-file suite option (import-shifts.test.mjs alone runs in 0.1 s) would make a campaign take seconds.

deviations.why: Step 4b asks for an automated guard; the defect class (guessing date order silently) has no reliable lint shape.

notes: Target import-shifts.mjs (changed on main 2026-11-13). Campaign 8 mutants, 2 caught; 6 gaps triaged and guarded; rerun 6/6 caught_after_fix. Real defect: day-first dates with no part >12 read month first; fixed with readDateOrder (span heuristic + notes). Verification: node --test 'ventures/shift-roster-builder/**/*.test.mjs' 449/449 pass; new test fails on the old code. The two real exports from eval/real-schedule-exports.mjs are not in the tree and were not re-run; both are settled by value so the new rule does not reach them. Possible follow-up: demand.mjs (--from-sales) could use the same span rule for short ambiguous files; it already prints a note.

real_defects.issue: A day-first schedule export whose dates all have both parts <= 12 (01/12/2026 .. 07/12/2026, the first 12 days of any month in a Deputy/UK/AU export) was read month first: 7 shifts became 7 'weeks', Monday and Saturday vanished, and no note said the order was a guess. Fixed: readDateOrder picks the order that keeps the dates closer together (and says so), and notes when a file cannot settle it.

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
